files_reviewed: Remaining components and dialogs (app-sidebar, add-member-to-team, create-tem-dialog, update/delete team and member dialogs, organization-list, team-card, team-list, organization-header, invitation table, edit-message-form, delete-message-dialog, leave-organization-dialog, menubar, navbar): grep for mutations, role gates, toasts, console.log, storage, env and localhost
note: No AI tools or tool calling. The two AI routes (compose rewrite and thread summary) run on the server with login, org check, a 2 per minute rate limit and a PII filter. Database is Postgres through Prisma on the server only, so no row level security labels apply. No prisma/migrations folder is committed. components/ui and .agents skill docs were skipped. The biggest gaps are the open PartyKit realtime server and routes that check the organization but not team membership.

labels.what: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in the committed example file holds a random-looking real value, not a placeholder. Secret value present. Anyone who copies it signs sessions with a public secret
DATABASE_URL in the example file includes a local Postgres password. Secret value present

PartyKit chat server accepts any WebSocket connection with no session or token check. Anyone who knows a team, thread or organization id can join that room and receive live message content and user emails
Server rebroadcasts any client-sent message:created, reply or presence event after schema parse only. A client can forge messages under another user's name, fake deletes or fake who is online
team.members.list looks up members by teamId alone, with no organization or team membership filter. Any logged-in user can list names and emails of any team by id
team.get finds the team by id with no organization check, so any logged-in user can read any team name
message.list checks that the team is in the active organization but not that the user belongs to the team. team.list only shows teams the user is in, so other teams' messages are readable by id
message.create lets any organization member post into any team in the organization, with no team membership check
message.threads.list returns a thread and all replies by id with only an organization check, no team membership check
AI thread summary loads any thread in the organization with no team membership check, so a non-member can get a summary of another team's thread

updateRole checks the caller is admin in the active organization but then acts on input.organizationId, and any admin may set the owner role. Only the better-auth call stands between this and privilege escalation
SendEmail is exported from a use server file, so Next.js treats it as a server action. It has no session check and sends from the app Gmail to any address with any subject and body
Email HTML is built by string interpolation with no escaping. Organization name and inviter name are user-controlled, so an attacker can inject HTML or phishing links into invite emails
Mail errors are caught and returned as success false, and sendInvitationEmail in lib/auth.ts lines 89-96 ignores the result. The UI says Invitation sent successfully even when no email went out
Outside production the email is only console.logged and success is returned, so staging builds without NODE_ENV=production never send invites
revokeSession and revokeOtherSessions ignore the error object the better-auth client returns, so the success toast shows even when the revoke failed
Full compiled thread text, with names and message content, is console.logged on every summary request
Invite input, including the invitee email, is console.logged
Messages written by other users are joined into the summary prompt with no prompt injection guard. detectPromptInjection is imported in lib/arcjet.ts but never used
Compose input is z.string() with no length cap before it goes to the model. Rate limit is 2 per minute but each call can be any size
Thread summary loads every reply with no limit and sends all of it to the model, so a long thread makes an unbounded prompt
Prompt says do not output HTML or images, but the compose preview renders raw model output with Streamdown and no image or HTML filter. Only the save path strips them through markdownToJson
Server accepts any string as message content, but the UI runs JSON.parse on it with no try. One non-JSON message sent through the RPC breaks the team message view for every member
imageUrl accepts any URL, not only the UploadThing host, so users can attach off-site images that next/image is not configured for
Auth allowedHosts trusts every *.vercel.app host, including other people's deployments
localhost:* allowed host and http://localhost:3000 fallback base URL are in the shared auth config, so they also apply in production
PartyKit host falls back to http://localhost:8787. NEXT_PUBLIC_PARTYKIT_HOST is not in lib/env.ts or .env.example
